content:
Nuevo Laredo will close its Día de Muertos observances tonight, Monday, November 2, with a music, art and tradition festival at the Panteón Municipal, starting at 7 p.m., according to municipal announcements reported by local outlets.

The evening is organized by the municipal government, under Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal, through its Directorate of Art and Culture, and is open to families gathering to remember loved ones and keep Mexican traditions alive.

The musical program features Jesús Armando and Trío Trova Nova, a group from Mérida, Yucatán, returning to Nuevo Laredo for a night dedicated to memory and Mexican roots.

At the center of the celebration will be a monumental altar dedicated to Coatlicue, a major figure in Mexica cosmology, accompanied by a pre-Hispanic-inspired ritual presentation involving girls learning and preserving those expressions.

The program also includes a tribute to singer Viola Trigo, who took part in Nuevo Laredo's Día de Muertos celebrations for 15 years, leaving a lasting mark on the city's cultural calendar, according to the announcements.

City cultural officials said the aim is to keep the meaning of Día de Muertos current and to bring new generations closer to the artistic expressions that form part of Mexican identity.

Sources:

title: Nuevo Laredo closes Día de Muertos tonight with Panteón Municipal festival at 7 p.m.
